newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India issues gasoline buy tenders due to shutdown.
newsitem.headline: India issues gasoline buy tenders due to shutdown.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has issued a two tenders to buy another two cargoes of gasoline in February to Goa and Kandla on the west coast due to refinery maintenance at Bombay, industry sources said on Tuesday.
One tender which seeks 25,000 tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for delivery February 15-19 will close January 22 with validity until January 24.
The other seeks the same cargo for delivery in the third week, February 21-25 and closes January 29 with validity until January 31.
IOC has already purchased a 25,000-tonne cargo, its first requirement for the month, for delivery February 8-12, in a tender that closed January 15.
"There is some shortfall in February because of maintenance work at a refinery in Bombay," one trader said.
Sources told Reuters state refiner Bombay Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) has planned to shut a 18,000 barrel-per-day fluid catalytic cracker in February for thirty days.
IOC has not finalised its purchase plan for March, sources said.
